## Summary

I implemented the soft-duplicate detection for `POST /api/owners` following the OfficeFloor function-injection pattern, keeping structural impact low by adding a new cohesive unit rather than growing any existing method.

**New behaviour (one small function class):**
- `DetectPossibleDuplicate.java` — mirrors the existing `CountNamesakes` step. It runs after the owner is built but before save (so it inspects only pre-existing owners), and flags the new owner `possibleDuplicate=true` / `possibleDuplicateOf=<id>` when another owner shares its last name (case-insensitive) and postcode but has a different telephone; otherwise sets `possibleDuplicate=false`.

**Wiring & plumbing (no existing method bodies changed):**
- `owners.POST.yml` — inserted a `detectPossibleDuplicate` step between `countNamesakes` and `save`, under the same `transaction` governance.
- `Owner.java` — added two persisted fields with fresh getters/setters (`possibleDuplicate`, `possibleDuplicateOf`).
- `openapi.yml` — added the two read-only fields to the `OwnerDto` schema; MapStruct maps them by name automatically (like `namesakeCount`), so `RespondWithOwner`/`RespondWithOwnerCreated` needed no edits.
- `db/hsqldb/schema.sql` + `data.sql` — added the two columns and padded the seed inserts with matching `NULL`s.

The hard-duplicate paths (`RejectDuplicateOwnerIdentity`, `RejectDuplicateHousehold`) are untouched, so a genuine duplicate still returns 409 before this step runs; only non-hard-duplicate household matches reach it and are created with the flag set.
